correctness.rationale: For p≡1 mod4, symmetric Legendre Seidel matrix on p finite indices has each four-subset triangle-sign product +1; switching leaves only three spectral classes: {3,−1,−1,−1}, {−3,1,1,1}, {±√5,±1}. Pair correlations of four triangle signs reduce to quadratic-character sum −1, giving total extreme number p(p−1)(p−3)(p−5)/96; nonsquare scaling equates extreme signs, hence each extreme count half of that and middle count binom(p,4)−2a. Thus δ4=1 for p=5 and 3/√p otherwise. Independent exact brute-force quadruple enumeration and Legendre signs matched p=5,13,17,29 and exact polynomial eigenvalue patterns; the proof covers all eligible primes and excludes infinity-index column explicitly.
